//: Which docs fopull.com publishes, in what order, under what heading. Read by scripts/build-docs-feed.sh, which emits the docs.json the website renders; see contracts/engine-site-feed.md in floptle-platform.
//why: Every page under docs/ is already public — the repo is open source — so this is not about secrecy. It is curation: a docs SITE is a finished surface, and this tree also holds the working material that got us here (handoffs, roadmaps, proposals, a checklist for one game's netcode). Publishing those alongside the guides makes the guides look like drafts.
//maintenance: A page's title and its one-line summary come from the page itself — the H1 and the first sentence — so adding a doc is not two jobs. What you must do is CLASSIFY it: `every_doc_is_classified` fails until a new file is listed here or in `internal`, and names the file. That failure is the point. Silence would mean a new guide never reaches the site, or an internal note quietly does.
//test: THE TEST A PAGE HAS TO PASS TO BE PUBLISHED: it helps somebody USE the engine, and it is TRUE TODAY. Both halves, and the second is the one that goes stale on its own — a page can be written to help and then quietly stop being true while nobody edits it. Things that fail it: design records, north stars, work plans, anything that opens by saying it is superseded or is not the current state, and anything whose subject has not been built. `no_published_page_disclaims_itself` in tests/docs_index.rs enforces as much of this as a machine can read — it fails a published page carrying the phrases those documents open with. It cannot tell whether a page is still true, so that half stays a person's job; when you make one internal, say WHICH half it failed in the line below.

internal.//: Working material. Public in the repo, deliberately not on the site — each line says why, because 'it wasn't on the list' is not a reason anybody can check later.
internal.README.md: the docs index — becomes the site's navigation, not a page in it
internal.news.md: reaches the site through the releases manifest's `news`, not as a docs page
internal.releases/: every version's notes already reach the site through the releases manifest, which carries them in full; re-publishing them as docs pages would be the same text at a second URL
internal.adr/: the two architecture decision records the shipped code cites by name, published so `// ADR-0028` in a source file resolves to something. Not on the site: two of the twenty-eight decisions on record would read as an incomplete set, and a docs site is a finished surface
internal.relay-bench.md: an operator's tool for sizing a region relay — how many players its link carries, and where packet loss starts. Same audience as fleet-agent.md: somebody RUNNING the service, not somebody making a game with it. A developer never needs it, and publishing a load-generator's manual alongside the tutorials would only invite people to point it at our relays
internal.fleet-agent.md: an operator's runbook for a Floptle Cloud region box — minting a box token, the systemd unit, what to read when a deployment will not start. It helps somebody RUN the service, not use the engine, and the audience is Fopull LLC plus anyone self-hosting a region; the page a game developer wants is multiplayer.md, which is published
internal.subsystems/README.md: folder index — the section heading covers it
internal.tutorials/README.md: folder index — the section heading covers it
internal.VISION.md: fails BOTH halves of the test above (`floptle/0190`). It is written to persuade a contributor rather than to help a user — it opens by telling the reader every decision in the repo should trace back to it — and it is out of date in the direction that undersells the engine: §7 still sets conditions for Floptle BECOMING a product it has met (three platforms, a paid cloud service, a shipped game), and §5 still calls networking `future` while fopull.com sells hosting for it. Kept in the repo, where the north star belongs; off the site, where a reader arriving from a search would be told the engine is not a product yet
internal.subsystems/networking-future.md: a design record whose first two paragraphs disclaim the rest of it — everything in it has shipped and its §7 stance was superseded by ADR-0022. Valuable in the repo as the record of why the seams are where they are; published, it is a click spent to be told that multiplayer.md is the page. multiplayer.md is that page and is published
internal.subsystems/physics-slices.md: a work plan, not documentation: slices ticked off as they landed, ordered by what is unit-testable versus what needs playtesting. Good project management, and it fails the first half of the test — it helps somebody BUILD the physics, not use it. physics.md is the page a user wants and is published
